title: Quant artifact reconstructability and catalog reversion procedure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Quantization artifacts for FP8/INT8 (profiles, calibration traces, and derived weights) are being produced by multiple calibration workflows and tool versions. We need a reproducible, auditable way to (1) deterministically reconstruct a quant artifact given inputs (model digest, calibration dataset snapshot, quant config, tool version), (2) emit a signed catalog entry with verifiable provenance, and (3) provide an operator-friendly rollback/reversion path when accuracy regressions are detected. This ticket scopes the design and implementation of an artifact reconstructability specification, a catalog schema with reversion semantics, and CI/validation hooks that gate artifacts into the release catalog. Outputs: hashing spec, KMS-backed signature process, catalog layout and APIs, CI checks including golden prompt accuracy harness, and an operator rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Hash spec documented: deterministic SHA-256 method that combines model_digest, sorted quant_config JSON, calibration_dataset_checksum, tool_version, and environment_digest
Signed catalog entries: artifacts are stored with a KMS-signed catalog record (catalog v2) and verification API returns signature validity
Reconstructability test harness: given model commit + quant_config + calibration snapshot the CI run reproduces the artifact hash within the same environment image
Golden prompt accuracy suite runs producing pass/fail per artifact with configurable delta thresholds; failing artifacts are auto-flagged and prevented from promotion
Rollback API implemented: catalog supports mark-deprecated and promote-previous operations; operator playbook documented and tested on staging
Observability: dashboard widget for artifact lineage, last-validated timestamp, and deployed fraction across dedicated fleets
